back: A relation that maps every element of the domain to exactly one output (one-one or many-one, never one-many).
Domain: the set of allowed inputs. Range: the set of outputs actually produced.
Different inputs give different outputs: $f(a) = f(b) \Rightarrow a = b$. Every horizontal line meets the graph at most once.
Surjective: the range equals the co-domain. Bijective: both injective (one-one) and surjective.
In $f : A \to B$, the set $B$ in which outputs are declared to lie; the range is a subset of $B$.

front: How do you find the range of a quadratic on a restricted domain?
back: Complete the square; if the vertex is in the domain it gives the least (or greatest) value; also evaluate both end points.

front: How do you make a quadratic one-one?
back: Restrict the domain to one side of the vertex: $x \geq h$ or $x \leq h$.
$0 < f(x) \leq \frac{1}{2}$: the value 0 is approached but never reached.
